implementation_notes: C has neither classes nor constructors, so the creation owner is a factory function: order_new(raw, &err) returns a pointer to an opaque struct order that is declared in the header but defined only in the .c file, which makes the function, not the struct layout, the only supported way to build the object; CERT's DCL12-C rule codifies exactly this opaque-type discipline. The classic factory class hierarchy has no C analogue: when the concrete creator must vary at runtime, a struct of function pointers (a hand-rolled vtable) replaces it, and a constructor function remains the entry point. Codebases on GLib get a library-provided alternative, because g_object_new() is a reflective factory keyed by GType with constructor/constructed hooks for post-property initialization.
pitfalls: If the struct definition leaks into a public header, callers can calloc or memset their own instances and bypass every check; keep it in the .c file or an internal header.
Failure must be one contract (NULL plus an out-parameter or errno, or a status code plus an out-pointer); mixing return conventions invites callers that check only half of them.
Ownership must be explicit per function (caller-owned results, borrowed arguments); every order_new needs a matching order_free or the opaque type leaks.

variants.name: GLib GObject reflective constructor
variants.implementation_notes: For code already on GLib the type system is the factory: register the domain type (G_DEFINE_TYPE), declare construction properties and let g_object_new(type, ...) allocate and initialize, with the constructed vfunc running after every construct property is set - that is where invariants depending on several properties belong. The domain factory then collapses into a wrapper function that maps raw data to construction properties, while GType supplies reflectively the which-concrete-type decision that plain C needs a hand-written table for.
pitfalls: Construction properties are set in a fixed order (construct-only first, then constructor, then constructed), so validation belongs in constructed; a property setter sees a half-configured object.
g_object_new returns a floating reference for GInitiallyUnowned types; sink it deliberately or the object is freed with its first container.
GType registration is global and one-shot; a failed registration cannot be retried in the same process.
